channel.title: CTF :: FAU Cyber Security Club
channel.description: CTFs (Capture the Flag) are structured hacking challenges. You find a hidden string called a flag by exploiting a vulnerability or solving a puzzle. They are the best low-stakes way to practice. This section covers where to start, how to approach challenges, and what categories exist.

item.title: Getting Started with CTFs
item.description: A CTF (Capture the Flag) is a security competition where you solve challenges to find a hidden string called a flag. Flags are usually formatted like flag{some_text_here}. They are the best way to apply what you have learned in a structured, consequence-free environment. Formats Jeopardy-style: A set of challenges across different categories. Solve a challenge, get a flag, earn points. You pick what to work on. Most beginner CTFs use this format.

item.title: CTF Categories
item.description: CTF challenges are grouped into categories. Each one requires different knowledge and tools. Pick one to start with and go deep. Web Web challenges involve attacking a website or web application. SQL injection, cross-site scripting, broken authentication, file inclusion, insecure deserialization — all of it shows up here. Start with: OWASP Juice Shop — a deliberately vulnerable web app you can run locally.
